items.title: Today Anthropic, PBC launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
items.detailText:
Today Anthropic, PBC launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
Today Anthropic, PBC launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
The proposed offering consists of 825,000,000 shares of Class A common stock. Of these, 801,351,354 shares are being offered by Anthropic and 23,648,646 shares are being offered by certain existing stockholders. Anthropic will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling stockholders. Anthropic also expects to grant the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 123,750,000 shares of its Class A common stock.
The initial public offering price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share. Anthropic has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “ANT.”
The proposed offering will be made only by means of a prospectus. Copies of the preliminary prospectus may be obtained from: Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 200 West Street, New York, NY 10282, by telephone at (866) 471-2526, or by email at prospectus-ny@ny.email.gs.com; or Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 180 Varick Street, 2nd Floor, New York, NY 10014.
Anthropic is a Public Benefit Corporation. Our mission is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.

items.title: Introducing Muse Spark 1.1
items.detailText:
Today, we’re excited to introduce Muse Spark 1.1, the latest model from Meta Superintelligence Labs and a significant upgrade from Muse Spark. Muse Spark 1.1 is a multimodal reasoning model built for agentic tasks, with major gains in tool and computer use, coding, and multimodal understanding.
With these improvements, Muse Spark 1.1 advances the performance-efficiency frontier. Together with this week’s launch of Muse Image , this release brings us closer to our vision of personal superintelligence: models that help you pursue your goals, create what you imagine, deepen your relationships, and take action on what you value most.
Along with this release, we are launching a public preview of the new Meta Model API where developers can access Muse Spark 1.1. The model is available now in "Thinking" mode in the Meta AI app and on meta.ai .
For more details about our evaluations, see our report .
Muse Spark 1.1 delivers exceptional performance in personal agentic tasks that require planning and orchestration across a range of external apps and services. It zero-shot generalizes to new native tools, MCP servers, and custom skills.
It tackles complex projects significantly faster than Muse Spark, as it is trained to orchestrate multi-agent systems to optimize end-to-end latency. As the main agent, it can gather context, make a plan, and delegate execution across parallel subagents. As a subagent, it adheres to its job, understands available tools, and knows when to escalate back to the main agent.
Muse Spark 1.1 can actively manage its context window of 1 million tokens. It remembers actions, retrieves information from much earlier work, and compacts in a way that keeps the critical steps needed for later work.
Muse Spark 1.1 excels at computer-use workflows that unfold across multiple applications with information changing on-the-fly. It maintains context across extended sessions, adapts to evolving requirements, and navigates unfamiliar interfaces with minimal human intervention.
Rather than reasoning through every desktop step one click at a time, Muse Spark 1.1 understands when to automate and when to use the interface directly. We trained the model to write scripts when automation is faster, click when direct interaction is simpler, and generate batches of actions at each step.
Agentic dinner party organization: In real-world applications, new context arises that changes the task. Muse Spark 1.1 notices these changes when placing the dinner order and makes necessary updates without user intervention.

items.title: Introducing Muse Image and Muse Video
items.detailText:
Muse Image follows instructions faithfully, edits with precision, composes from multiple references, and draws on Instagram for social context. Muse...
We’re excited to launch Muse Image and preview Muse Video, the first media generation models developed by Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Image is our most advanced image generation model yet: it follows instructions faithfully, edits with precision, and composes from multiple references. It also brings agentic tool use capabilities and integrates with Muse Spark. Muse Video, built on the same pretraining base, delivers exceptional visual fidelity with native audio support.
Muse Image is available today across the Meta AI app and on meta.ai , Instagram Stories in the US, and WhatsApp in limited countries, and is coming soon to Facebook. Muse Video is coming soon to creators and Meta AI.
Instead of directly mapping prompts to images, Muse Image operates as an agent: it invokes search and coding tools to improve accuracy, self-refines its own generations, and improves through scaling test-time compute. Muse Image also integrates with Muse Spark, allowing the two models to share tools and plan jointly for powerful agentic media generation.
We provide Muse Image with access to tools to enhance its agentic capabilities.
Coding. During reinforcement learning, Muse Image learns to write and execute code that produces accurate plots and QR codes, and condition on rendered figures to improve the accuracy of generated images. Muse Spark and Muse Image also integrate to use the combination of code and media generation to create animated GIFs, websites with embedded images, and interactive visual games.
Search. Muse Image learns to search the web to ground generated images in factual and real-time information and visual references. Enabling search improves factual accuracy on knowledge-intensive prompts, particularly those involving current events and real-world facts.
Muse Image improves with search tool use. Win rate from internal ablation.
Muse Image reflects on and improves upon its own work within its chain of thought. This self-refining behavior can take different forms: a local edit to the current image draft when a small detail is off, a new image generation from scratch when larger parts are wrong, or a different tactic like tool use for more factually accurate generation. We didn’t design this behavior. Instead, it emerged during RL training simply because self-refinement produced better images and therefore higher reward.
Muse Image improves with emergent self-refinement. Win rate from internal ablation.
Muse Image improves with scaling test-time compute. Elo from internal ablation.
Muse Image edits images with precision, changing exactly what the user asks for. It can follow a variety of instruction

items.description: Alibaba Cloud DevOps AI Assistant Update: AI at Every Stage of DevOps Collaboration This article introduces the updated Alibaba Cloud DevOps AI Assistant, which provides automated, context-aware support across the entire software developmen
items.detailText:
This article introduces the updated Alibaba Cloud DevOps AI Assistant, which provides automated, context-aware support across the entire software development lifecycle.
Before we begin: If you already use Alibaba Cloud DevOps to manage requirements, code, and pipelines, this update is worth a few minutes of your time to get reacquainted with your "new colleague." It requires no separate login or switching between tools. Instead, it is embedded directly in the pages you open every day, covering key stages of development collaboration, from requirement entry, test case generation, and code review to pipeline troubleshooting and release decisions.
Alibaba Cloud DevOps AI Assistant requires no separate login; its capabilities are built into the various pages of Alibaba Cloud DevOps. It runs through the core development collaboration workflow:
In a nutshell: tell it what you want to achieve in natural language, and it gets the work done in the pages you already know.
Alibaba Cloud DevOps AI Assistant currently has three entry points, serving three types of needs: asking questions directly, using features with one click in context, and running tasks automatically in the background.
An "AI Assistant" icon appears at the top of Alibaba Cloud DevOps pages. Click it to open the chat dialog. Whatever page you are on, you can ask questions directly in natural language and have it help you complete your work.
In addition to the entry point at the top of the page, Alibaba Cloud DevOps embeds AI buttons directly in many feature-specific scenarios, such as improving requirement content on the requirement details page, troubleshooting errors on the pipeline page, and fixing issues with one click on the code scan results page. Clicking a button automatically supplies the current context and prompt, so you do not have to formulate your request from scratch.
Under "AI Assistant Tasks" in your Alibaba Cloud DevOps personal workbench, you can turn frequently repeated work into automated tasks. For example, you can automatically generate a summary of the previous day's progress before each morning meeting, summarize work hours every Friday, or automatically trigger content optimization when a requirement's status changes. Once configured, AI Assistant runs in the background as planned and delivers the results directly to your chosen destination: email, DingTalk, or Feishu.

items.title: Alibaba Cloud Launches Full-stack AgenticOps, Making the Agent the First User in Operations and R&D
items.description: Alibaba Cloud Launches Full-stack AgenticOps, Making the Agent the First User in Operations and R&D This article introduces Alibaba Cloud's full-stack AgenticOps platform, enabling autonomous, closed-loop AI operations and R&D through
items.detailText:
This article introduces Alibaba Cloud's full-stack AgenticOps platform, enabling autonomous, closed-loop AI operations and R&D through unified observability, evaluation, and controlled execution.
The upgraded Cloud Monitor 2.0, now with agentic observability, makes both the system and Agents legible. A complete Agent task breaks into three consecutive phases: trusted facts, evidence-based judgment, and controlled action. For observability by Agents, Cloud Monitor 2.0 hands production facts to the Agent through a single pipeline.
For governance, the observability pipeline runs through three stages — standardization, organization, and trustworthiness — turning raw observability data such as metrics, logs, traces, events, and metadata into production facts that carry their source, freshness, semantics, quality, and cost boundaries.
Once Agents can evolve themselves, the moat in enterprise AI shifts from whose model is better to whose evolution flywheel spins faster.
That chain rests on a unified operational context. Unified Connectors reach across Alibaba Cloud accounts, enterprise IDCs, and external systems; unified data modeling then brings metrics, logs, traces, events, changes, and code together with applications, instances, containers, and databases into one context that an Agent can understand and investigate.
Cloud Monitor 2.0, AgentLoop, STAROps, and Alibaba Cloud DevOps are product capabilities for enterprise production. Beyond them, Alibaba Cloud contributes to three open-source projects — OpenTelemetry (OTel), UModel, and BRiSE — to break, at the foundation, the three walls of data that cannot be collected, context that cannot be understood, and capabilities that cannot be verified, so the whole stack becomes a public asset the industry can reuse, verify, and build together.
When a system can perceive, decide, and turn every resolution into experience for the next one, the competitive question in enterprise AI becomes simple: who evolves faster.

items.title: AgentScope Service: Open-Source Agent Control Plane with DeepSeek Harness Support
items.description: AgentScope Service: Open-Source Agent Control Plane with DeepSeek Harness Support This article introduces AgentScope Service, an open-source control plane for managing and orchestrating diverse enterprise AI agents. Alibaba Cloud Native Com
items.detailText:
This article introduces AgentScope Service, an open-source control plane for managing and orchestrating diverse enterprise AI agents.
The AgentScope Java community has released the AgentScope Service component as open source. Its design positioning is broadly aligned with the open-source Python version. Targeting enterprise-grade distributed Agent scenarios, its control-plane components provide multi-tenancy, visual debugging, and multi-Agent orchestration for Agents on the AgentScope data plane.
AgentScope Service also supports integrating Agents in various forms, including Claude, DeepSeek Harness, and Langchain.
AgentScope Service provides an open-source solution for Agent debugging and distributed deployment. If you need enterprise-grade Agent orchestration, Teams orchestration, observability, evaluation, and other capabilities, visit the Alibaba Cloud AgentTeams and AgentLoop product pages.
AgentScope Service does not aim to replace your existing Agent framework. Instead, it provides a unified control plane for centrally managing Agents built with different frameworks and technology stacks, such as Claude, OpenClaw, and QwenPaw.
Today, there are many options for building enterprise-grade Agents. As an excellent Agent Framework, AgentScope offers enterprises a complete solution for building Agents. However, a traditional Agent Framework is no longer the only way to build Agents. Coding Agent products are expanding into more domains, and using tools such as Claude SDK and Qoder CLI to build enterprise-grade Agents is becoming a choice for many enterprise users.
These approaches are not mutually exclusive. Within one company, R&D may use Coding Agents, the business middle platform may use AgentScope, and new projects may prefer a managed Harness from the outset. This is common. AgentScope Service is not tied to any Agent framework or platform; it provides unified management and control for all Agent runtimes.
Control Plane is the core component of AgentScope Service. All Agent applications register centrally through the control plane. SDK or Sidecar integration supports registration and connectivity for mainstream Agent Frameworks (AgentScope, LangChain, ADK), as well as Claude, Qoder, and others.
Dashboard is the control plane's visual UI console. It provides cluster-wide observability information, including online agent lists, deployment instance details, active session information, and token consumption, making it easy to understand how the cluster is operating.
You can also view session information in the dashboard, inspect the real-time context state of active sessions (the proportions of data in each section), dynamically adjust or compact session context, intervene in sessions, and more.

items.title: 陈宇森携阿里千问办公推企业级AI Agent落地
items.detailText:
陈宇森携阿里千问办公推企业级AI Agent落地
2026年6月，在杭州郊外的半亩水田里，马云、吴泳铭等阿里合伙人挽起裤脚，在泥地里插秧。
接任钉钉CEO第一周，陈宇森向内部发了一封全员信，取消了钉钉强制晚9点的复盘会，也废除了早会签到和深夜巡岗。阿里传统的管理偏向过程管控与高能见度，而技术出身的陈宇森，更习惯用自动化工具减少重复劳动。
阿里不缺模型、算力和云基础设施，缺的是把这些能力变成企业愿意使用的Agent产品。
这并不是他第一次面对企业客户。十二年前，他第一次创业时，就曾在这个问题上碰过壁。
2014年，中国移动互联网进入快速扩张期。那一年，手机网民规模达到5.27亿，手机上网比例首次超过PC。移动支付、手游、电商等应用迅速生长，大批年轻技术人员开始寻找创业机会。
陈宇森就在这一年从浙江大学毕业。他没有选择阿里等大厂，反而和几位“蓝莲花”战队成员在北京创办长亭科技，进入企业级网络安全领域。
大学期间，陈宇森多次在国际安全赛事中取得名次。长亭科技成立后，他亲自跑客户，拿着安全赛事世界冠军的履历去见银行负责人，相信领先的技术指标足以说服对方。
银行客户关心的不是技术有多先进，他们在意是否满足业务规则、合规要求，能不能解决实际问题。于是，陈宇森开始把精力从展示技术转向理解客户，长亭科技的业务也逐渐打开。
2015年，长亭获得真格基金天使轮融资。到2018年，全国多家头部银行，陆续成为长亭的客户。
2018年，阿里云升级为阿里云智能事业群，业务重心从基础算力供给延伸到更复杂的企业服务。
第一次创业的成功，让他完成了从技术人员到企业服务创业者的转变。但成功也带来另一种错觉：只要技术和学习能力足够强，换一个行业也能快速跑通。
这次，他同时创办了两家公司：薮猫科技继续做数据安全，2022年完成由源码资本领投的数千万人民币A轮融资；“交给猫吧”则尝试将AI与图形学结合，开发中大型游戏。
数据安全公司的进展顺利，游戏项目却没能跑出来。2023年，因为资金消耗和方向偏离，游戏公司不得不关停。
他后来在第一财经的采访中反思，自己当时对陌生行业缺乏敬畏，试图用过去的成功经验，直接做一个在玩法和题材上都有创新的中大型项目，却低估了游戏行业的常识壁垒。
长亭科技的成功，让他相信技术能力可以快速跨界；游戏项目的失败，则让他意识到，技术可以缩短试错时间，却无法替代对行业的理解。
2023年底，陈宇森回到阿里。这一次，他没有直接进入核心产品线，而是先担任集团CEO办公室研究员。
2024年4月，他转入阿里云，负责全球战略合作伙伴业务，兼任拉美区域总经理，参与南美市场从零开始的建设。
对于一个经历过两次创业的人来说，技术浪潮带来的兴奋感已经不够了。他需要找到一个更具体的答案：模型能力不断增强，究竟能改变什么工作？又有什么产品值得用户持续付费？
阿里的 通义千问 加速研发。到了 2025 年 2 月，Hugging Face 开源榜单上，大量头部模型基于 Qwen 系列二次训练，Qwen 成为开源生态里不可忽视的力量。
他先后尝试了Vibe Coding产品“瓦特”、面向Agent的应用市场，以及内部测试的PM Agent。这些产品要么没有发布，要么在测试阶段被推翻。
原因并不复杂，许多应用只是给模型套上新的交互界面，能快速做出来，却很难让用户持续使用。
直到2024年Cognition推出Devin，陈宇森看到了一个不同的方向：AI开始具备操作电脑、编写代码并执行复杂任务的能力。它不再只是回答问题，还可以接手一段具体的工作流程。
2025年，他在阿里云内部带队孵化了AI Agent产品MuleRun（骡子快跑）。
在这个精简的团队里，陈宇森做了一次自动化实验，团队与AI讨论需求后，由AI在后台编写代码、运行测试。MuleRun 没有做大规模投放，上线不久就收获来自全球 43 个国家的付费用户，其中 34% 的高价值月付用户，单月付费额度在 200 美元以上。
这次尝试让陈宇森看到，AI的价值不只在于提高人的工作效率，还可能改变完成工作的方式： 一个小团队可以借助Agent承担过去需要更多人力完成的任务。
但个人或小团队的自动化实验，只是第一步。要把Agent放进一家大型企业，面对的将是更复杂的数据、流程和组织关系。
2026 年 7 月，阿里启动内部整合，把 Qoder Work、悟空、MuleRun 三条分散的 Agent 产品线收拢，8 月 3 日 千问 办公正式公测发布，陈宇森担任 千问 办公CEO。
但摆在他面前的是棘手的结构性矛盾，钉钉过去十几年的商业底盘，建立在席位订阅之上，企业按人头采购账号，人越多，账单越高。Agent 的核心价值，恰恰是承接重复、标准化的岗位工作，压缩人力操作流程。
一旦 Agent 深度嵌入核心业务，就有可能侵蚀存量订阅收入，如果要保住稳定的 SaaS 基本盘，Agent 又只能停留在文档润色、会议摘要这类低风险辅助场景，很难真正触达经营内核。
9月底杭州的云栖大会上，他提出了一个问题：我们公司上个季度华东区的毛利率是多少？
通用模型不知道“我们公司”指谁，也不知道企业内部的数据分布和财务口径。模型可以解释毛利率，却未必能找到一家公司的真实经营数据。
陈宇森用一句话概括自己的判断： Context is All You Need。
这让他重新回到长亭科技时期遇到的问题。技术能力再强，也不能跳过客户自身的业务规则。只不过当年的产品需要理解银行的安全需求，如今的Agent需要理解一家企业的数据、岗位和工作流程。
企业不会因为Agent能够完成任务，就把核心系统的权限交给它。哪些数据可以读取，哪些操作可以执行，出现异常能否追溯，都必须在产品设计之初考虑清楚。
为了让企业敢于让AI处理业务，做安全起家的陈宇森，在产品设计上找回了当年的敬畏。
千问 办公推出了“企业上下文”，将150PB的企业数据进行逐层解析并建立知识图谱，让Agent在执行任务时只匹配最需要的几万个Token，同时，安全中心将沙箱机制、全程审计和最小权限体系强行接入了Agent。
在 11 月推出的 千问 办公 2.0 版本，进一步把定位从个人 AI 办公助手升级为面向个人与组织协作的 Team Agent（团队智能体），重心向组织协同倾斜。
今天的陈宇森，不再只是为一家创业公司寻找生存空间，而是承载着阿里集团在AI时代通往企业级市场的全新入口。
几个月前，在杭州郊外的那半亩水田里，马云、吴泳铭等阿里合伙人光着脚，在泥地里插秧。
老阿里的农耕信仰，强调亲自下场、肯下笨功夫，相信多流汗才能换来粮食。陈宇森的极客信仰，则是用代码和自动化减少无谓的人力消耗，让AI接手重复劳动。
插秧需要耐心，让AI进入企业也需要耐心。前者要把秧苗种进

items.detailText:
Aditya Mulik shares how Walmart scaled resilient multi-agent LLM batch workflows across 4,700 stores, cutting monthly inference costs by 90% while enforcing semantic validation and bounded retries.
A monthly overview of things you need to know as an architect or aspiring architect.
Facilitating the Spread of Knowledge and Innovation in Professional Software Development
Unlock the full InfoQ experience by logging in! Stay updated with your favorite authors and topics, engage with content, and download exclusive resources.
Lily Mara explains how to avoid high-risk software rewrites through incremental FFI refactoring. She shares how engineering teams can replace Python bottlenecks with Rust via PyO3, demonstrating how to achieve dramatic function-level speedups, seamless integration testing, and meaningful infrastructure cost savings without microservice overhead.
Agentic AI architecture extends microservices and cloud-native architectures with AI agents that work with context, memory, and protocols such as MCP and A2A. The article covers bounded-context integration, task-dependent coordination strategies, new security risks, and observability needs. It expects gradual adoption alongside existing architectures, with platforms absorbing common components.
Aditya Mulik explains how Walmart Global Tech deployed multi-agent LLM workflows across 4,700 stores for nightly batch inventory forecasting. He discusses tackling production hurdles - schema violations, cross-department data mismatches, and network drops - via MCP grounding and loop agents, while slashing cloud inference costs from $100k+ to $10k per month shifting from PTUs to pay-as-you-go.
Vanessa Formicola shares how technical leaders can move beyond "wishful architecture" by practicing holistic socio-technical engineering. She discusses why engineering leaders must account for organizational maturity, reward structures, geopolitical climate, and team dynamics, framing the staff-plus role as designing the conditions for technology to thrive rather than just picking tools.
Oli Lane and Julian Wreford share how Gearset replaced guesswork in distributed asynchronous queues with OpenTelemetry tracing. They explain why traditional metrics fall short, how to implement user-centric SLOs based on latency distributions, and share practical debugging tips to help senior developers, software architects, and engineering leaders improve system reliability and team culture.

items.title: Expanding our partnership with GSA to bring Claude to all levels of government
items.detailText:
Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.
We are expanding our partnership with the General Services Administration (GSA) through a new agreement that gives government partners a 40% discount on Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API. For the first time, the discount applies across every product surface, including when agencies buy from us directly today and through cloud providers in the coming months. The discount also extends to state, local, tribal and territorial governments.
We are also launching a dedicated program to help agencies implement and make the most of their Claude use. These programs are commonly leveraged by our private sector customers and we’re looking forward to bringing those best practices to our public sector partners in the coming weeks.
The discounts offered through the agreement are estimated to save the government $1 billion. Agencies are not bound by a minimum spend commitment and will be able to pay for the usage they consume.
Government agencies are using Claude to solve some of their most important challenges. Examples include managing backlogs, records and forms, and modernizing old code. Some of the ways agencies are using Claude include:
Agencies can use Claude for their most sensitive unclassified work. Claude for Government, which delivers Claude's coding and agentic work capabilities and provides near-feature parity with commercial offerings at a FedRAMP High authorization level, was made generally available on September 30.
Agencies building their own tools can use Claude through Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud’s Vertex AI. On Bedrock, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High, with select models authorized for DoD IL4 and IL5 workloads in AWS GovCloud. On Vertex AI, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High.
Claude Enterprise is in process for FedRAMP Moderate authorization through the FedRAMP 20x program, marking the next evolution of how we are bringing the same innovative technology available commercially to the government.
Government agencies can buy Claude at the OneGov discount through GSA's Multiple Award Schedule today. Whether your department or agency already uses Claude or is interested in using it, our Public Sector team will help discuss your options.
Anthropic is a Public Benefit Corporation. Our mission is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.
